headline: Janmashtami, marking Lord Krishna's birth, is celebrated nationwide with religious fervor today
summary: The auspicious occasion commemorates the advent of Lord Krishna approximately 5,500 years ago, who descended to Earth to establish righteousness and vanquish evil.
details: Today marks 'Shubho Janmashtami', the auspicious appearance day and religious festival of Lord Sree Krishna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for the Sanatan Hindu community. The day is being observed nationwide with due religious solemnity, grandeur, and a festive atmosphere, and is a public holiday across the country.

According to Sanatan scriptures, Lord Sree Krishna appeared on Earth approximately 5,500 years ago in the Dvapara Yuga, on the Ashtami Tithi of the Krishna Paksha in the month of Bhadra, under the Rohini Nakshatra. At that time, the tyrannical King Kamsa's cruel rule in Mathura made life miserable for common people and ascetics.

A divine prophecy foretold Kamsa's death at the hands of Devaki's eighth child. Fearing this, Kamsa imprisoned his sister Devaki and brother-in-law Vasudeva, brutally killing their first seven newborns.

Finally, on a dark, stormy night in Bhadra, the Supreme Lord Sree Krishna appeared as their eighth child in the prison. By divine instruction, Vasudeva carried the newborn Krishna in a basket over his head, crossing the turbulent Yamuna River to safely reach Gokul in Vrindavan, where he was secretly raised under the loving care of Nanda Maharaj and Mother Yashoda.

Though he performed childhood pastimes as 'Gopal', the butter thief and cowherd boy, in adulthood, he destroyed tyrannical forces by slaying Kamsa. Later, in the Mahabharata's Kurukshetra war, Sree Krishna became the charioteer of Pandava hero Arjuna, delivering the ultimate guide for humanity, the 'Srimad Bhagavad Gita'.

In a famous verse from the Gita, he declared, "Yada Yada Hi Dharmasya Glanir Bhavati Bharata, Abhyutthanam Adharmasya Tad Atmanam Srijamyaham," meaning, "Whenever righteousness declines and unrighteousness prevails, I manifest Myself to protect the virtuous, destroy the wicked, and re-establish truth."

On this occasion, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir and Prime Minister Tarique Rahman have extended heartfelt greetings and congratulations to all citizens, including the Sanatan community, through separate messages. Bangladesh Television, Bangladesh Betar, and private satellite TV channels are broadcasting special programs, while national dailies feature informative special articles.

Across the country, including Dhaka, various monasteries, temples, and puja mandaps are hosting day-long processions, Gita Yagnas, Sree Krishna Puja, Kirtans, Aratis, Prasad distribution, and religious discussions. In Dhaka, the Mahanagar Sarbajanin Puja Committee has organized a two-day central Janmashtami festival at Dhakeshwari National Temple.

The festival began today at 8 AM with a Gita Yagna for the welfare of the nation, conducted by the Sankar Math and Mission of Sitakunda, Chattogram. A colorful central Janmashtami procession will commence at 3 PM from Palashi Mor, near Dhakeshwari Temple, proceeding through various old Dhaka roads and concluding at Bahadur Shah Park. Special Sree Krishna Puja will be held at night.

Today, Sree Krishna's teachings of love, devotion, selfless action, and standing against injustice remain the eternal foundation of life philosophy and faith for millions of Sanatan devotees worldwide.

headline_marked: [[Bangladesh government faces rising expenditure]] in salaries, fuel, and debt, while revenue growth lags
headline: Bangladesh government faces rising expenditure in salaries, fuel, and debt, while revenue growth lags
summary: The government's financial management faces significant challenges as nearly 42% of the 2026-27 budget is allocated to non-revenue generating sectors like salaries, debt repayment, and subsidies, with revenue collection struggling to keep pace.
details: Bangladesh's government is grappling with escalating expenditures across multiple sectors, including the implementation of a new pay scale, debt servicing, subsidies, and increased fuel costs. These rising expenses are coupled with a limited growth in government revenue, creating a significant financial challenge.

Approximately 42% of the proposed BDT 9.38 trillion budget for the 2026-27 fiscal year is earmarked for government employee salaries, pensions, debt interest payments, and subsidies. These three sectors alone account for nearly BDT 4 trillion, consuming almost half of the government's annual spending.

The full implementation of the new pay scale is projected to add an extra BDT 1.05 trillion annually to the government's expenditure. Concurrently, the government is relying on budget support from the World Bank to manage the costs of importing fuel and fertilizers.

The National Board of Revenue (NBR) faces an ambitious target of collecting BDT 6.04 trillion in the current fiscal year, requiring a 45% growth in revenue. This growth rate is significantly higher than past achievements, intensifying the pressure on the government's financial management.

Economists are advising the government to review its spending priorities and reduce expenditures, given the limited opportunities for revenue growth. Dr. Mustafizur Rahman of CPD highlighted the dual pressure on the economy from global trade conditions and inherited issues, stressing the need for careful prioritization to avoid increasing the debt burden.

The new pay scale for government employees includes a 100% to 142% increase in salaries, to be implemented in four phases. In the current fiscal year, employees will receive 70-75% of the increased basic salary in two installments, with the Ministry of Finance currently calculating the exact cost implications.

The energy sector is in turmoil, marked by nationwide load shedding, limited industrial production due to gas shortages, and rising international fuel prices exacerbated by the Middle East crisis. Importing liquefied natural gas (LNG) is becoming riskier due to increased costs and supply chain issues.

The government owes private power producers BDT 44 billion and provides substantial subsidies in this sector. LNG prices have surged from $22-24 to $28 per unit, nearly double the price before the Iran conflict, further increasing the government's subsidy burden.

Subsidies for fuel, fertilizers, and other sectors are projected to cost BDT 895.39 billion in the current fiscal year. The global increase in oil and LNG prices is pushing these costs even higher, with crude oil prices now at $95 per barrel, up from $70-75 before the Iran conflict.

To support farmers, the government subsidizes fertilizers, 80-85% of which are imported to meet the annual demand of 6.7 million tons. Supply chain disruptions from the Middle East crisis and rising international prices have further increased the cost of these imports. Bangladesh secured $300 million in emergency budget support from the World Bank in June to import 600,000 tons of fertilizer by April 2027.
